title: Related species with shared constitution produce analogous variations

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Related species with shared constitution produce analogous variations

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Species that inherit nearly the same constitution from a common parent and are exposed to similar influences tend to produce analogous variations, so that a variety of one species may resemble another species of the same genus.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Species inheriting nearly the same constitution from a common parent and exposed to similar influences will naturally tend to present analogous variations

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter V, “Laws of Variation”; section “Species of the same genus vary in an analogous manner.”. Scope: species within a genus, domestic races and wild species

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch05-17: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.57

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Parallel variation has clear comparative predictions and can be tested in selected radiations. Public data are scattered and seldom contain identical environmental exposures across an adequate phylogenetic design.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Under matched environmental perturbations, compare the direction and type of heritable phenotypic variation among close versus distant relatives. Greater parallel variation among close relatives, and resemblance of variants to congeneric species, supports the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Matched perturbation datasets across several related species are uncommon.

Similar phenotypes may reflect shared environment rather than inherited constitution.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Parallel variation among congeners is measurable in a set of well-sequenced groups, and public sequences plus association catalogs cover those models. There is no general table of analogous varieties across genera, so the scope is partial. Selection in similar conditions and shared genetic constraint both predict the pattern, and they can be separated only where the genes are known.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare the axes of within-species variation among congeners, and ask whether a variant of one species phenocopies a trait typical of another, using both morphology and parallel genetic changes. Correlated axes beyond those of distant species would support the claim; uncorrelated variation once shared environments are controlled would refute a general tendency to analogous variation.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Analogous variants are documented in case studies rather than a cross-genus database.

Domestic races are better measured than wild congeners.

Shared environments can produce parallel variation without a shared inherited constitution.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

data existence: 0.56
discriminating power: 0.54
operationalizability: 0.64
analysis feasibility: 0.52
